_READ_FIRST: games/the_balance/process/README.md — THIS GAME OVERRIDES THE SKILL. The Want is SIX things and holds nothing countable (if the game can count it, it is a system). The board does NOT run as one lump or as a fixed block queue: it runs as STEPS agreed one at a time, and the OPENING was step 2 (sheets/OPENING.md), before systems, places and people. Our step page says WHAT for this game; the skill says HOW — never copy the skill's rules into games/the_balance/process/. Guards are one page per step and CARRIED.md rows falling, not a stop count. Verdict boxes are two, not four. Tier rungs start at 5 not 15. Anything LO reads obeys the readability rules in section 5. Cut Want material lives in process/CARRIED.md — consume it, do not re-derive it. games/orientation is off-limits by LO's explicit instruction. Read that file before acting, and again at the top of every step. Keep this key alive in every edit to this file.

want.who_she_is: Nell, 18. Her mother married Gil Barnes three years ago and the house came with him, with his son Nate, 20, and his daughter Tasha, 21. She has just started at the college on the other side of town, and she is the only person in that house who is going anywhere. What she has to lose: nobody here has revised their picture of her since she was fifteen.
want.obligation: Gil paid her tuition. She pays him back weekly and it is most of an honest week's work. It never finishes — the next semester posts. And Lynn does not know he paid. NUMBERS AND MECHANISM: process/CARRIED.md §4-§6, owned by block 1 S3.
want.appetite: To be looked at by people who were not supposed to be looking, and to be the one who decided they would. It cannot complete: every room she gets into has a room behind it, and the camera supplies strangers faster than she can use them. Where the hold stops being the reason — the Friday the debt is clear and she sets the phone against the books and goes live anyway.

why_this_person.npc_gil: he paid for her and has never once mentioned it, and she cannot work out whether that is decency or a debt she has not been shown the size of
why_this_person.npc_nate: a senior at her college who was fine before she moved in. He cannot stand her, and underneath it he wants her — hiding that is the only thing he is good at, and her climb with him is making him show it
why_this_person.npc_tasha: two years ahead and already does all of it without apology. She is what the player is being shown she could be. She laughs at Nell; she cannot out her
why_this_person.npc_lynn: not wanted — she is the price tag. Every hour Gil is not in the kitchen is an hour Lynn is on a ward, and that is what makes it cost
why_this_person.npc_owen: he decides what her week is worth, in hours, and he is the first person to want something from her that was not free
why_this_person.npc_hale: the one man whose approval is worth something on paper, and the only person on that campus who can hand her money that is not a shift
why_this_person.npc_sam: In her class, her age, and the ONLY person in the game she is the one who wants. Every other climb is somebody wanting her; this one runs the other way, and until he existed she had no want of her own anywhere. Everybody likes him, which is the mechanic and not the flavour: being seen with him is worth something and losing him is visible to people who are not her. He is the ordinary life she is trading away and the person she has to lie to - the only cost in this game with no money attached. He says no by BELIEVING her. First build: talking, and that is all.
why_this_person.npc_cara: Her friend, and the only person in the game who wants nothing off her. She wants her TIME - the one thing Nell is running out of - so she is a cost where everyone else is a payer, which is what makes dropping her the cheapest hour to free up and what makes it hurt. She is the other end of the phone: the messages in talk.md are hers. She says no by going quiet, never by confronting.
why_this_person.npc_reyes: he is the consequence. A strict officer who wants nothing from her, which is what makes him different from every other man in the game
why_this_person.npc_jules: she runs the crowd and she is the one making Nell small, so being pushed around and being let in are the same channel. She does not giggle — she assesses, which makes a dare read as a test that can be passed. She is a target in the end
why_this_person.npc_bree: not wanted — she is the crowd's mouth, the one who says the cruel thing out loud. Thin on purpose
why_this_person.npc_paige: not wanted — lovely to her face, and she lets Bree do the talking. Thin on purpose

want.world: A college town. The house on the near side, the campus across town, the strip downtown where the cafe is.

WANT.md cut from 4,203 words to 586, over eight rounds with LO. The stopping rule is his: if the game can count it, it is a system; the Want holds what the game IS. Six items survive — who she is, the appetite, the world, the charge, the eight people, second person. None is countable.

The start choice is DELETED, not deferred. It was three difficulty settings dressed as memories. The freedom=25.9% figure that justified it means freedom DURING PLAY ('farmer, slave merchant, bounty hunter... you can be whatever you want'), not a three-way pick at minute zero — and this game already has that. The creation screen's relationship picker remains.

The debt and the four meters were reclassified as SYSTEMS and left the Want. Both were defended and then conceded: a debt is a number, and meters are systems by definition. Only the situation stays — she owes her step dad and her mum doesn't know.

Three of the four Gil constraints became structural rather than written rules: his ladder has no self-opening rungs (so he cannot initiate — there is no mechanism), the income rungs clear the debt (arithmetic), and the build already prints his explicit rank. 'Strict and does not drink' moved into his cast line because it is who he is.

process/CARRIED.md created as a TEMPORARY holding file. The cut only simplifies the Want if every cut item lands somewhere that will build it; if it lands nowhere we deleted the game. A row is deleted when its block consumes it; the file is deleted when the last row goes.

2026-09-12, LO: the board runs as STEPS, not as a fixed block queue. Agree what a step holds, write The Balance's one page for it, two boxes, next. The division is his: OUR step says WHAT (the room, the hour, the person, the choice); the SKILL says HOW. My first draft of the opening step was five items that were all the skill's checklist reworded; a copy rots when the skill changes and it makes him read an engine checklist to review a story decision.

The opening moved from block 4 to step 2, ahead of systems/places/people. Reason: it is the most concrete question in the game and it CREATES the rooms and people it needs, where an abstract step drifts vague (S1 asked for everything the game tracks before one thing had been decided). Coverage is the cost and CARRIED.md plus the Want's eight people are the checklist against it.

sheets/OPENING.md written and approved in principle by LO before writing. Cold open naming nobody: bedroom (18 today, step dad paid the tuition, first payment Friday, mum does not know) -> hallway (shower, a closed door, mum's bag gone) -> hands over into the kitchen about 07:30 with Gil at the table, the chore list on the fridge and a bus in twenty minutes. First free choice is chore-for-money vs eat with him vs leave early: money against time on the first click. A staged open was rejected because it puts the collector on screen one as the game's first face.

Next-step rule, 2026-09-12: blocked first, then whatever the most things wait on, else what the player sees next. The queue is the tail of each sheet (what it hands to the steps after it) — no separate to-do file. The ORDER is per-game; only the loop, the rule, the tail and one-page-per-step carry between games. LO left the END of the step list open deliberately ('no end is fine for now'); the risk is recorded in process/README.md §2.

sheets/systems/money.md written. $2,400 a semester, $150 every Friday, sixteen weeks clears it, next semester posts for more. Three earners at the first build (cafe, going live, chores capped) with Hale's reading, Tasha's parties/bar and the till/pawn held for later releases — six routes cut to three so each is deep. Ignition not tax: week one is two short shifts (under $150) and by about week four a clean week is ~$220, so honest work covers the settle with ~$70 left. Missing a Friday rolls over: the cost is social (he asks in front of Lynn) and then the house rules tighten for a week. lynn_knows write-list closed to four writers. CARRIED rows 4, 5, 7 and the arithmetic half of 6 consumed.

sheets/places/the_house.md written. Nine rooms: her bedroom, the landing, kitchen, living room, bathroom, Nate's room, Tasha's room, the master bedroom, the garage. LO named the living room (rest + TV), the master bedroom, the step brother's room and the shared bathroom as must-haves, and ruled Tasha lives at home. Three of them carry systems rather than scenery: the living room is the free hour, the two bedroom doors are the walk-ins, the bathroom is `clean` and the lock. The landing is built as the door junction, not as a corridor. Chores landed here because the chores are here: bins, laundry, dishes, the car, $5 each, one paid a day (~$35 a week — real in week one, pocket change by week four). Gil's three rules are wired to objects: the front door after ten, her bedroom door open when anyone is on the landing (the same door the stream needs shut), the list before she leaves.

sheets/places/the_cafe.md written, LO's shape. Three places: the cafe (one room — no separate floor, the counter is a spot not a location), the office out back (Owen's, LOCKED at the first build and the door the first release ends on), and a COMMON toilet shared with customers. Two ladders on one place, deliberately different shapes: customers are many/shallow/cash (a hand not moved, showing more, the toilet for money — asked for with TIPS, ~$10/$30/$80, LO's addition) and Owen is one man/deep/pays in hours and access (tables, counter, closing, keys, opens alone). PROMOTION NEEDS BOTH KEYS — shifts worked AND how far she has gone with him — because adult-only promotion makes the waitress work pointless and turns the cafe into a menu. Customer cash is the fastest money in the game, so its brakes are declared here: only some customers, only when the room allows, always costs cover. Shift ~5 hours; week one two shifts ~$110 (under the $150), by week four four or five for ~$220.

sheets/systems/the_week.md written — the clock, taken next because the opening, the house and the cafe were all written and all three were stuck on it. Wake 07:00, game starts 07:30, no forced bedtime. Classes 09:00-12:00 weekdays; three cafe shifts that CANNOT all be had: early 07:00-12:00 costs a class, middle 12:00-17:00 fits, closing 17:00-22:00 breaks Gil's ten o'clock rule and is the shift where Owen is the only other person in the building. House presence: Gil kitchen till eight and back by six, garage late; Lynn nights on the ward three times a week (so the master bedroom is only live on the nights she is home); Nate almost always in; Tasha in at four, out Friday and Saturday nights. House quietest on weekday afternoons, fullest Sunday. Friday's $150 is handed over in the kitchen at six. Bus 40 minutes and $2 each way, walking an hour, a lift from Gil free and a favour. Owen confirmed male at LO's call before this.

sheets/systems/the_phone.md written. Messages + camera app only at the first build; no bank, map, job board or battery; paid tier is a later release. ONE place to go live at first — her own room with the door shut, deliberately the same door Gil's rule keeps open, so the stream is wired to a house rule from session one. Needs clean + alone + an hour. Pays ~$20 early (less than a shift, more than a chore, one hour not five), $50+ once she has regulars. Cost is cover and nothing buys it back; as cover falls she starts being recognized in the street, which OPENS content rather than only punishing. Best hours are weekday afternoons and after the house sleeps — the same hours the cafe wants, so the two earners compete for the same clock. Dane and Reyes are both already watching and she does not know.

LO's revision to the phone, same day: it is a STREAMING app, not a camera app, and the payout is a RANGE rolled per session, not a flat number — $8-25 starting out, $20-60 with a few regulars, $50-120 known. FOLLOWERS lift the range and rise when she streams and further when she does something new. Two consequences taken with it: the player cannot compute how many sessions clear Friday (the settle is fixed, the income is not), and followers/cover become two one-way numbers moving in opposite directions off the same act — followers never fall (reward stacking), cover never returns (price stacking).

No subscription model in this game at all, LO's call — not deferred, dropped. People FOLLOW her (free) and every stream pays on the night, with the roll's range lifted by the follower count. Corrected in the phone sheet, money sheet, DECISIONS.md Q4 and Reyes's line (he pays her on stream, he is not a subscriber), and in CARRIED's motel row. Earlier entries in this log that say 'camera app' or 'paid tier' are superseded by this one.

LO: the follower count is SHOWN to her, on the app screen. Taken with two consequences. (1) The payout bands become visible thresholds — under 500 / 500 / 2,000 — so the next band is a door she can see, which is the release doctrine's shape applied to a number. (2) It cannot start at zero: the Want already says Reyes has been paying her since March, so she has been streaming quietly since the summer to a few hundred people who have never seen her face, and that is why one of them already knows her name. Recommended and flagged to the meters step: followers are a number she sees, cover is NOT — cover should read as words, or the player farms it.

sheets/systems/her_meters.md written — Q1 answered ON HER, not per-person, and the page says so in the open so LO can overrule it there. Four: nerve (caught-able places and hours), appetite (what she takes and whether she asks), standing (campus reach — it delivers people and almost never refuses), cover (renamed from `anonymous`, only falls, and falling OPENS being recognized as much as it shuts being casual). `audience` DELETED as a fifth meter: it meant how many are watching, which is the follower count already visible on the phone — one idea, one number. Nerve/appetite/standing display as WORDS not scores (a number invites farming); followers stay a number because she is meant to watch it climb. Needs kept: rest and clean, with clean gating going live. Rungs start at 5 per O3; what sits at each step is deliberately NOT decided here. CARRIED rows 1, 2 and 3 consumed; the bottom/top door lists stay in CARRIED for the places and scenes steps.

LO 2026-09-13: cover is CUT and the rest renamed — nerve -> exposure, appetite -> corruption, standing -> reputation. Three meters, not four. Exposure absorbs what cover/`anonymous` measured: it is both how far into the open she will go AND how much of her has been seen, so it climbs and never comes back, and being recognized still opens content instead of only punishing. All three names clear the 27-game vocabulary check (corruption is the field's most-read system). Propagated to her_meters, the_phone, money, the_cafe, DECISIONS row 5 and CARRIED. Nothing is built, so no saves break.

Cast cut from eight to SEVEN, LO 2026-09-13. Dane is gone: 'dont add customers as NPCs', so cafe customers stay faceless and the tips ladder runs on strangers. Nate rewritten — a senior at her college, hostile, who wants her underneath and hides it; her climb is making him show it, and the walk-in is where it first cracks. He is now in BOTH her worlds (house and campus), so 'almost always in' is corrected on the house and week pages. Tasha can no longer out her (contradicted the Want; the Want line is rewritten) — she is the example and the supplier, not a threat. Owen is a STRICT boss and his office is NOT locked, so the first release's visible locked door moves to the CLOSING SHIFT — the schedule with her name not on it, and the hours when the cafe is him and her. Reyes no longer pays her: the 'since March' line also put him paying a seventeen-year-old, and LO chose simple — a strict officer, consequence only, wanting nothing from her.

sheets/people/the_cast.md written — seven blocks, six lines each: what they want, where they are, what they give, how they refuse. Gil's block carries the structural rule in the open (he never opens a step; every step with him is one she opens). Nate is the biggest ladder in the house — from cannot stand her to showing it — and he is the only character in both her worlds. Owen refuses by giving the shift to somebody else, never by threatening. Hale's lever is marks, which need attendance, which needs sleep, so he is wired to the needs. Reyes is a threat with NO trigger yet and the page says so.

Campus built as a WORLD, not a corridor, over four rounds with LO. sheets/places/the_campus.md: nine places, all open at the first build — quad (the root, where being known is READ), lecture hall (a hundred people, only the sheet knows she came), classroom (a dozen, Hale in the room, undone homework is visible), department, library, union, gym, a FRIEND'S DORM ROOM (LO said yes — the only private room on campus she can be invited into), and the row. THE ROW IS CAMPUS-SIDE at LO's call: being known pays off within walking distance of where it was earned, and the way home is through the park against a ten o'clock. Two teaching rooms, not five identical ones, because they apply different pressure. LO refused a campus restroom and refused any campus earner: every campus hour is hours and bus fare going out, which is what makes the cafe and the phone the only ways out of Friday.

sheets/systems/college.md. Campus measures two things that fight each other — marks and being known — and her hours only stretch to one while the cafe eats them too. Marks: classes 9-12, Hale sets and grades everything, exams week 8 and finals week 16 on the SAME sixteen weeks that clear the debt. The teeth cost nothing to build: if she fails, Gil's money was wasted, and the warning letter after bad exams goes TO THE HOUSE — the cheapest route in the game to losing the secret about who paid. Being known: two crowds (the crowd, and the serious ones), she starts outside both, and THE CROWD CAN SHUT HER OUT — a door that never closes is not a door. Three activities only, each passing LO's test that it must move a meter and put her in a room with someone: parties at the row (dares are the climb), the gym, and posing for the art class (looked at on purpose by people who are allowed to — pays standing, not money). Clubs, study groups and sign-up sheets refused by name.

LO 2026-09-13, two corrections to campus. (1) The friend's DORM ROOM is removed — campus now has eight places and NO private room at all, so everything there happens where someone could walk past. (2) Teaching is not Hale-only: four subjects, four teachers, attendance and marks counted PER SUBJECT so she can be fine in one class and sinking in another. Hale teaches one of the four — his is the one where being liked changes the number — and the other three are names on a timetable that can each become a real character in a later release.

sheets/systems/walking_in.md — LO's campus brainstorm landed as ONE mechanic reused in both halves of the game rather than a campus cast. She walks in on people: at home two doors she knows (Nate, the master bedroom on the nights Lynn is in it), on campus strangers in six rooms (library third floor after eight, gym showers, the department corridor once empty, a classroom between classes, behind the row houses, the quad late) who need no names. WHAT CLIMBS IS HER REACTION, NOT HER ACTIONS: back out / freeze / stay and watch / let herself be seen / be spoken to / be asked in. LO's addition: the menu is gated by CORRUPTION — low, watching is not on offer at all — and taking the furthest thing available is what raises it, so the ladder climbs itself and nothing is ground. Split of the two meters falls out: corruption is how far she will go, exposure is what it costs when she is seen. First walk-in is written for her with no choice offered; locked options are SHOWN as a line, never hidden, which is how the meters stay readable with no number on screen. The engine already does walk-ins as chance rules banded on corruption, so this needs no new machinery.

sheets/systems/being_known.md split out of college.md (which hit 680 words against our own one-page rule; now 304 and 458). LO's combine: THE GIRL WHO RUNS THE CROWD IS ALSO THE ONE MAKING HER SMALL, with her friends, on the quad. So being pushed around and being let in are the same channel — every dare is a humiliation and an invitation and the player cannot take one without the other. Three rules keep it a climb instead of cruelty: every round visibly moves her closer, she can always walk away at a cost in standing, and getting in does not end it. Her friends are in Nate's year so campus and house stop being two games, and she ends up a target herself — the only thread between two women. Cut from my own earlier proposal, which LO rejected wholesale: four archetype names (the friend, the queen bee, Nate's mate, the watcher), rivalry as its own system, bullies as separate people. A boyfriend is HELD, and if he ever comes in he comes in as an alibi, not a romance. Gossip is now required, not optional: without something telling her where people are she goes to class and goes home and no walk-in happens.

sheets/SYSTEMS.md — the master list, written LAST instead of first, at LO's prompting ('many things here can be its own systems'). Done as a COLLECTION job from the eight pages already written, which is why it works now: at the start it would have been guesswork, and that is exactly the S1-first ordering LO threw out. 22 tracked things in seven groups. Three findings the list caught and no single page could: (1) GOSSIP HAS NO SOURCE — two pages depend on her knowing where people are and nothing produces it, so the campus walk-ins never fire; (2) four systems are fed in ONE place and read everywhere — followers (phone), shifts and the move up (cafe), marks (class), standing with the crowd (quad/row) — which is the property night_desk's six ambient systems lacked; (3) two candidates to cut: `streams done` duplicates followers, `dares taken` duplicates standing with the crowd.

sheets/systems/talk.md — the hole SYSTEMS.md caught, closed the same day. One system, not two, because both halves come from the same act (standing somewhere and listening): it tells her WHERE PEOPLE ARE (which is what makes the campus walk-ins and the parties reachable instead of blind luck) and it tells her WHAT PEOPLE SAY ABOUT HER (which is how reputation and exposure become visible with no number on screen). Six sources: union tables, the minutes before class, the quad, the gym locker room, the row, her messages. Costs her a few minutes — listening is chosen, not ambient wallpaper. Three rules keep it a rumour: it goes stale (tonight means tonight), it is sometimes wrong, and it sharpens as she climbs until somebody is describing a room she recognizes. Declared cost: it is a lot of small writing that must change as she does.

Jules named and written into the cast (21, runs the crowd). Chosen over Bree and Paige for the lead because the design hangs on a dare reading as a TEST rather than a joke — she watches, decides and is usually right — and because the later reversal, when she is the one being looked at, needs someone worth waiting for. The two rejected names became her two: Bree says the cruel thing out loud, Paige is lovely to her face and lets Bree do it. Both deliberately THIN — the crowd's voice, not two more ladders — and both in Nate's year, which is how the quad gets home before Nell does. Cast page renamed from THE SEVEN to THE CAST: eight written, two thin.

The first build is HER FIRST FOUR WEEKS, written to sheets/RELEASE.md. Reached by the picking rule running out: every remaining tail row is the same kind of work (steps, scenes, lines), nothing is blocked on a decision, so the next question is necessarily what ships and what waits. Four weeks is not arbitrary - money.md already fixed it: the build has to reach about week four or the squeeze never lifts on screen. IN: the opening as written; the house (nine rooms, chores, Gil's rules, two doors with one step each); the cafe (room + toilet, two shifts rising to four, two customer steps, the move up to the counter); the phone (going live in her room, followers, the pay range); campus THIN (classes, quad, union, talk, Jules's first two dares); eight people. OUT: gym, library, department, art class, the row on a party night, Hale beyond a name, the three other teachers, Reyes, the letter home, exams, the one who recognizes her. ENDS ON: the closing shift - visible on the schedule from week one, her name not on it, and it needs BOTH keys (shifts worked and how far she has gone with Owen). Campus is in rather than held because the whole point of the game is that college is what changes her; a first build without it is a game about a girl with two jobs. It is thin because every campus room wants talk lines plus a walk-in at three heights, which is the largest pile of writing in the design.

sheets/RELEASE.md proposes the FINISH LINE for the step list, which LO left deliberately open on 2026-09-12 ('no end is fine for now') and which process/README.md says is his to close, not ours. The proposal: the step list ends when the six rows of what-is-in have a page each, and nothing else. Pending his tick on the two boxes. Also mapped RELEASE -> kind 'decision' in scripts/notion_sheets_sync.py FILE_KIND so the page sorts first in the review order instead of last as an untyped sheet.

CARA added - the friend, the ninth name. Chosen over Mae (quiet) and Priya (organized) because the loss has to be LEGIBLE and only a talker going quiet is legible: the message thread visibly thins. Her job is structural, not warm - with nobody on Nell's side, nothing she loses reads as a loss, and she is the one claim on Nell's HOURS in a game where every other person pays her. She also fills a hole talk.md had: 'her messages' was one of six sources of talk with nobody on the other end. In the first build she only ever repeats what the crowd says and never knows it is true; finding out is a later build. WHY THE PROSE KEEPS COMING OUT COMPRESSED - THE ROOT CAUSE, 2026-09-16. LO asked twice, and the second time in plain words: not "fix it" but "what is causing this?". THREE FORCES, ALL PUSHING THE SAME WAY, AND NOTHING IN THE BUILD PUSHES BACK. (1) EVERY WRITING THRESHOLD IS A MAXIMUM. gates.py:7390 is the whole thing in one line - gate("sentence length", ... med_sent <= SENTENCE_CEILING, ...). It passes MORE comfortably the shorter you write; a median of 3 words clears it by the widest margin available. Same direction for DASH_CEILING, NARRATION_DIALOGUE_CEILING, MENU_CEILING, FIELD_NEGATION_MAX. ⚠️ SAY IT PRECISELY: the claim is no floor on sentence-level READABILITY, not "no floors at all" - EXPLICIT_BEAT_FLOOR and EXPLICIT_BEAT_MEDIA_FLOOR are real floors on explicit content and media, and MEDIAN_LOCATION_WORDS is a volume target that 3,000 words of fragments clears. Grepping gates.py for `too short`, `sentence_floor`, `min_words`, `finite verb` or `antecedent` returns nothing. So cutting a word always improves the score or leaves it flat, and nothing has ever told this repo it went too far. (2) THE BEAT BUDGET MAKES GRAMMAR THE CHEAPEST CUT. 35-40 words per beat is correct and measured (register.md:387), but the subject and the verb are the cheapest words to lose because they carry no INFORMATION: "You turned eighteen last month." (5w) -> "Eighteen last month." (3w). The fact survives, the sentence does not, nothing measures the sentence. (3) CAVEMAN ULTRA BLEEDS FROM CHAT INTO THE BEAT. CLAUDE.md:60 puts this repo's CHAT in a register that drops articles and likes fragments; CLAUDE.md:86 already says "A beat is persisted text. Compression has never governed a beat and must not start." The prose is written in the same session as the chat and it leaks - "Eighteen last month." IS caveman ultra, rendered to a player.
